case.pattern_description: A coordinated low-and-slow micro-authorization attack involving repeated online charges under $10 (product C) spaced across days and weeks, rather than a rapid card-testing burst. The pattern affects at least 20 customer cards concurrently without subsequent large purchases. This indicates automated micro-billing exploitation or distributed card validation across accounts rather than standard card-not-present fraud.

evidence.claim: Customer reported: Customer C12975 message: 'I did not make these charges on my card. Please look into it.' Refers to 3660260.

Card C12975-K2 made 6 online product-C charges totalling $23.99 over 21.2 days (3660255, 3660256, 3660257, 3660258, 3660259, 3660260); in its 60 transactions of the 60 days before, that kind made up 0%. Every one is a tiny authorisation, spread over days with no larger purchase after them, so they are not R5's sequence of three within an hour followed by a purchase.

20 other cards (20 other customers) newly show the same signature in the 30 days to the alert - 3+ online authorisations under $10, on a card that had not made such charges before - against 8 and 4 in the same window one and two months earlier: C05083-K1, C09471-K2, C00348-K1, C08972-K1, C12223-K1, C03611-K2, C12030-K1, C09582-K1, C01326-K2, C10035-K2, C05704-K2, C04528-K1.

evidence.claim: Card C12975-K2 experienced an activity shift with a run of six online micro-authorizations under $10 for product C totaling $23.99 between 2017-01-05 and 2017-01-26 (txns 3660255, 3660256, 3660257, 3660258, 3660259, 3660260), completely deviating from the 60-txn baseline which had zero product C charges.

Holder baseline analysis for C12975-K2|337|194 shows zero prior transactions and confirms the flagged $2.90 charge has fewer than two prior similar charges, failing to match any established recurring charge pattern.
Card C12975-K2 was previously subject to confirmed fraud in closed case CC-4890 in October 2016 where 2 online transactions totaling $800.03 were confirmed as card-not-present fraud.

Device D000168, used in related micro-charge 3660259, is a generic Internet Explorer 11 desktop browser profile seen across 480 cards and linked to 41 closed cases (37 confirmed fraud), representing weak non-specific device risk.
Flagged transaction 3660260 scored 0.0 on the fraud model with an estimated historical fraud rate of 0.0063 and a low risk score of 0.04, indicating no real-time model detection.
Billing region 337 is an established region for card C12975-K2 with 28 prior transactions, and shared origin analysis for region 337 shows an unremarkable fraud lift of 0.14 vs all transactions.

The alert text also contained 2 segment(s) addressed to the system rather than an analyst (outcome_directive, override, role_marker). They were set aside and used neither as evidence nor as instruction; the decision rests on the evidence above.

case.summary: Cardholder C12975 reported unauthorized activity on card C12975-K2 regarding disputed transaction 3660260. An investigation identified six unauthorized online micro-authorizations for product C totaling $23.99 between January 5 and January 26, 2017, completely deviating from the card's in-person retail baseline. Network graph analysis confirmed an identical micro-billing pattern surging across 20 other customer accounts during the same period, indicating a coordinated multi-customer abuse scheme. The card was confirmed compromised under an undocumented fraud pattern, prompting card blocking, monitoring of connected accounts, and filing of a regulatory report.

sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details a coordinated online micro-authorization abuse scheme affecting customer C12975 and card C12975-K2. Between January 5, 2017, and January 26, 2017, six unauthorized card-not-present transactions totaling $23.99 were processed for product C in billing regions 191 and 337. The unauthorized charges include transactions 3660255 ($3.51), 3660256 ($5.18), 3660257 ($2.66), 3660258 ($4.75), 3660259 ($4.99), and 3660260 ($2.90). Customer C12975 reported transaction 3660260 as fraudulent and denied making the purchases. Prior to these events, the card baseline consisted exclusively of in-person retail purchases with zero online product C history. Transaction 3660259 was conducted using device D000168, associated with an Internet Explorer 11 desktop browser profile. The card previously suffered confirmed card-not-present fraud under closed case CC-4890 in October 2016. Graph analysis revealed the identical micro-billing pattern active across 20 other customer cards during the same thirty-day period, including C05083-K1, C09471-K2, and C00348-K1. Scheme peer activity surged from four cards two months prior to twenty cards currently, confirming widespread coordinated testing or abuse. The bank blocked card C12975-K2 and initiated monitoring across all identified connected cards.

stop_reason: The investigation stopped pursuant to policy section 6 because the fraud probability reached a decisive level of 0.966 supported by multiple independent incriminating findings, including the customer dispute, a sharp baseline behavioral anomaly, and cross-card graph links establishing coordinated scheme activity, such that further inquiry would not change the disposition.
